import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter for the latest registration year to avoid duplicate entries for the same dog
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# Ensure 'KreisLang' is a string and handle potential NaN if any (though unlikely for district names)
df_latest['KreisLang'] = df_latest['KreisLang'].astype(str)

# Aggregate the number of dogs by district and gender
# We count unique HIDs per district and gender to represent distinct dogs
# If HID is not a unique dog identifier across years, then just counting rows (len(df_latest)) for each group is fine
# Given the task description and sample, each row seems to represent a dog registration instance.
# So, counting occurrences of (KreisLang, SexHundLang) pairs is appropriate.
dog_counts = df_latest.groupby(['KreisLang', 'SexHundLang']).size().reset_index(name='Anzahl Hunde')

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a grouped bar chart
sns.barplot(
    data=dog_counts,
    x='KreisLang',
    y='Anzahl Hunde',
    hue='SexHundLang',
    palette='viridis'
)

# Add labels and title
plt.title(f'Number of Dogs by District and Gender in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('District (Kreis)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', title_fontsize='12', fontsize='10', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
